newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's NAB profit seen weaker.
newsitem.headline: Australia's NAB profit seen weaker.

text.p: Australia's most profitable bank, National Australia Bank (NAB), is forecast to report on Thursday a weaker or, at best, flat quarterly earnings result.
Banking analysts told Reuters on Wednesday they expected NAB to report net profit of between A$530 million and A$560 million for the third quarter ended June 30.
This compares with A$560 million for the second quarter ended March and A$582 million for the first quarter. A year ago, NAB reported A$505 million for the third quarter.
NAB, like the rest of the banking sector, has begun to feel the squeeze on interest income from intense competition in the domestic home loan market, the analysts said.
An investment bank's analyst said NAB's interest margins were forecast to shrink by 22 basis points in its second half-year ending September 30, compared with the first half.
"I think a flat result will be taken by the market to be good," said the analyst, who declined to be identified.
He has forecast a third-quarter net profit of A$560 million for the three months to June 30.
ABN AMRO Hoare Govett banking analyst Michael Pulman said he expected NAB to report a net profit, after goodwill, of A$536 million for the third quarter.
"I think the expectation is the second half (of the 1996/97 year) will be a bit worse than the first," Pulman said.
He has forecast a full-year net profit of A$2.225 billion before abnormal items, reflecting a weaker second half. NAB reported first-half earnings of A$1.14 billion.
"The trend is of slightly declining earnings," Pulman said.
In 1995/96, NAB reported net annual profit of A$2.1 billion.
Adding to the squeeze on margins, NAB'S bad debts are expected to creep up in the current half-year, analysts said.
The investment bank's analyst forecast total bad debt provisions to rise to A$113 million in the second half-year, up from A$105 million in the first half.
"Bad debts are starting to trend up," he said.
NAB's tax bill is also expected to be higher in the current half-year, but analysts said a weaker Australian dollar and stronger sterling would make its British earnings look better.
NAB owns four banks in Britain, Northern Ireland and Ireland, and two banks in the United States and New Zealand.
"We expect there should be more signs the bank's interest margins are being squeezed but its offshore operations should continue to show (earnings) growth," a Sydney-based bank analyst told Reuters.
